chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih Al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the bone-exposing injury (al-mudhiha) in the head, just as it is in the face. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The bone-exposing injury and the fracture in the face and the head are equal in the wergild (diyah), because the face is part of the head, and the injuries in the body are not like those in the head.'

key_terms.الشِّجَاجُ: Fracture or breaking of the bone
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةُ: A specific type of injury where the bone is exposed

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in wergild for head injuries versus body injuries in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the face is anatomically and legally subsumed under the head for the purpose of wergild (diyah), establishing that injuries exposing bone in either location incur identical compensation. It further distinguishes cranial injuries from general bodily wounds, highlighting the specific jurisprudential valuation of the head in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the precision of Imami legal reasoning in categorizing bodily parts for financial reparation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih Al Sowry, 
(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about

Al-Mowziha (bone exposing injury) is like what is in the face. So heasws said: ‘The bone-exposing injury, and the fracture in the face and the head are equal regarding the wergild, because the face is from the head, and there is none from the injuries in the body like it is in the head’.
